0|b0e9a2fe3ff971950833bc0ffc383babd9443bc4|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"sctp: add support for SCTP_REUSE_PORT sockopt
This feature is actually already supported by sk->sk_reuse which can be
set by socket level opt SO_REUSEADDR. But it's not working exactly as
RFC6458 demands in section 8.1.27
- This option only supports one-to-one style SCTP sockets
- This socket option must not be used after calling bind()
or sctp_bindx().
Besides
column2: SCTP_REUSE_PORT sockopt should be provided for user's programs.

column1: Otherwise
column2: the programs with SCTP_REUSE_PORT from other systems will not

column1: work in linux.
To separate it from the socket level version
sctp_sock and it works pretty much as sk->sk_reuse
setup limitations that are needed when it is being enabled.
It should be noted that the behavior of the socket-level socket option
to reuse ports and/or addresses for SCTP sockets is unspecified""
leaves SO_REUSEADDR as is for the compatibility.
Note that the name SCTP_REUSE_PORT is somewhat confusing
functionality is nearly identical to SO_REUSEADDR
extra restrictions. Here it uses 'reuse' in sctp_sock instead of
'reuseport'. As for sk->sk_reuseport support for SCTP
added in another patch.
Thanks to Neil to make this clear.
- add sctp_sk->reuse to separate it from the socket level version.
- improve changelog according to Marcelo's suggestion.
